Any type of learning in which you mean to shape your behaviors starts within the framework of understanding emotions, their inter-relationships and the factors which instigate or dispel them. If you understand what gives rise to your motivation, you can to some effect control it.

First, self-discipline is rather attached to motivation if you didn't know.

Second, motivation is often a perceived solution to a perceived problem. (There's a deeper secret behind this, but it will ruin petty motivations, which is what I'm sure you're after, unless your goal is self-enlightenment).

Simply said, the easiest way to kickstart motivation is to find something you feel like you NEED. Or at least very strongly desire. The caveat is it has to be realistic enough that you believe you can achieve it. Setting reasonable goals towards very desired objectives and you can manufacture motivation for self-discipline.

30 Days of Discipline. Short self-help ebook but extremely effective if you genuinely want to rapidly become a more disciplined person. Gives you 12 habits to pick up by performing them every day for 30 days, such as waking up early, taking a cold shower, exercising, having a to do list, etc. Only real way to learn is by doing and this book gets straight to it.
